a-census-copied-a-title-no-item-has.claim: tests/census.json shipped GO-143's first-attempt title under registry_version b0abf2819da0, which a registry carrying that title does not hash to, so the content and the stamp came from different registries and the stamp was the only field the suite read. Both recorded ledgers now have every field they copy from the registry re-read on each run, in a reading that is itself witnessed field by field.

a-greek-rho-killed-the-evidence-layer.claim: subprocess.run(text=True) decoded a child's output with the platform's ANSI codepage, so one Greek rho (cf 81, and 0x81 is unmapped in cp1252) killed the reader thread, left stdout None and reported an AttributeError. The child half could not encode raw UTF-8 at all without PYTHONIOENCODING. Both are pinned to UTF-8 and a dead reader now reports itself.

a-loop-past-the-tenth-hop-is-no-loop.claim: The cap is a named constant with a basis, and the walk that stops at it removes has_loop rather than answering False, so CI-014 reports NO_DATA on a chain nobody followed to its end.

a-mostly-refused-run-reports-a-clean-cou.claim: A run where almost every image was unchecked no longer reports broken_image_count at all; the key is absent, which the runner reads as NO_DATA. No share was needed — a clean count over an incomplete check is withheld at any share, and a non-zero one always stands.

a-placeholder-in-structured-data-almost-.claim: An unfilled template published in structured data is a warning, and neither item reading the script can fail on one: MS-032 asserts errors and its warn band is only consulted when that assertion has already failed, and GO-143 catches a placeholder only on a WebSite node. The SearchAction case GO-143 used to catch by accident left with its old pattern in 0.89.0.

a-run-under-a-ported-host-cannot-be-file.claim: `history_path` files a run under `os.getcwd()/.seo-runs/<netloc>` with the netloc used verbatim, so a URL carrying a port produces a directory name containing a colon. Windows rejects that component and `os.makedirs` raises after the audit has already finished, losing the run; Linux and macOS accept it. `previous_run` and `run_series` build the same path. Unseen for eighteen releases because every runner invocation in the suite and in all six in ci.yml passes `--no-history`.

a-truncated-crawl-decides-the-whole-site.claim: Twenty items — eleven of them `high` — asserted a clean verdict over an input their own script had capped; the runner now withholds the PASS and leaves the FAIL alone, across all six ways this registry spells `none of these`.

answer-block-score-and-the-parser.why: A closed narrative about a parser-dependent verdict, held by the test that asserts the two parsers agree.

article-seo-private-answers.claim: article_seo.py takes the shared author and publication-date answers; no HTML fixture disagrees with them, and neither class-matched shape produces a name or a date.

cache-cleanup-test-claimed-the-machine.why: A closed narrative about a test repair, held by the test itself.

ci-002-scope-and-title.claim: CI-002 is retitled to what one inspected URL can answer; inspecting a set of important URLs is still not built.

measured.title: Confirm Google Has Indexed the Audited URL

ci-019-and-cn-053.claim: Both items closed, CI-019 in 0.21.0 and CN-053 in 0.22.0.
ci-019-and-cn-053.why: A closed narrative. What it says stays open is a lesson about how the sweeps find things, not a defect a probe can reproduce.

class-named-comments-are-invisible.claim: A byline inside a container named only by class is read as the page's author.

cn-068-floor-and-the-good-fixture.claim: Closed in 0.87.0: the floor moved from 60 to 35, the sum of the components eeat_signal_checker awards that a page of any type can carry. Five items in this class reported FAIL on both fixture origins and now separate them.

credit-boundary-ignores-itemref.claim: A byline a comment claims through itemref, directly or along a chain, is no longer read as the page own; a byline two items both claim stays withheld, and a byline nothing claims is untouched.

default-locale-route-tree.why: A closed narrative about a release, held by the hreflang tests it added.

duplicate-twin-items.why: A closed narrative about the report's own weighting, held by the report tests.

eeat-vocabulary-by-declared-language.claim: Three reviewed vocabularies ship — English, Lithuanian and Russian — and a page declaring any other language is read with the English one, marker for marker.

entity-checker-reads-the-graph-unbounded.claim: GEO-006 is graded on entities extracted with no foreign-credit boundary and a top-level-only scan: a reviewed organisation's four links pass it, the page's own publisher nested one level does not reach it, and a reviewed Product is not an entity type at all.

foreign-credit-keys-width.claim: The boundary is ten keys wide, and the author of a book the page is only about is still read as the page's own.

four-rulings-closed.claim: All four rulings closed in 0.25.0 and 0.26.0.
four-rulings-closed.why: A closed narrative about four registry repairs, held by their assertions.

freshness-and-foreign-dates.claim: A date inside a container named only by class or by microformats is still read as the page's own, while the declared itemprop spelling is filtered.

go-138-nondeterminism-as-first-written.claim: Superseded by the entry above it, which diagnosed the cause.
go-138-nondeterminism-as-first-written.why: Kept deliberately as the entry the diagnosis replaced. Probing it would probe the entry above.

go-138-was-never-a-flake.claim: GO-138's rule no longer matches a pattern at all: 0.93.0 moved it to `invalid_url_count`, so neither the port of a test origin nor a URL containing `404` can reach it. The `field` narrowing this entry is about was the 0.19.1 repair and is now moot for this item.

go-143-asked-for-a-claim-that-was-not-tr.claim: GO-143 failed any page whose WebSite node lacked potentialAction, so its remedy was to publish a SearchAction naming a search endpoint the site may not have — for the Sitelinks Search Box, which Google removed from Search on 21 November 2024. Retitled to the live feature the assertion measures: the WebSite node Google reads for the site name.

measured.title: Complete Every WebSite Node Google Reads for the Site Name

gsc-scenarios-accepted-a-dead-rule.why: A closed narrative about a test repair, held by the scenarios it rewrote.

gsc-thresholds-uncalibrated.claim: Nine Search Console numbers keep their inherited values and are deliberately not relabelled measured.

image-inventory-count-on-a-page-with-no-.why: A closed narrative about a release. Its repair is held by the tests that release added, not by this file.

items-that-could-not-fail.claim: Closed in 0.50.0; the severity_vocabulary mechanism that closed it proves no item today, against the seven it named when it shipped.

kw-071-evidence-and-title.claim: KW-071 asserts summary.contested_queries eq 0 with a warn band at lte 3, and no item in the registry names the removed worst_spread this entry was written about.

measured.title: Is there evidence of keyword duplication or overuse?

line-wrapped-minified-css.claim: The pinned corpus has a minified file at 37.13 bytes per line and an authored one at 47.09, so no bytes-per-line boundary separates them.

macos-kills-a-forked-child.claim: Closed in 0.15.0 as three AST-checked rules over every subprocess call.
macos-kills-a-forked-child.why: A closed narrative. The three rules it ends with are a test in this suite, which is the reader that keeps it true.

one-test-robots-answers-another.claim: The state directory is read from SEO_RATE_LIMIT_DIR on every use rather than captured in a module constant, so a child process inherits it; the suite names its own and its fixture servers drop their origin answer when they stop.

pacing-test-never-forked.why: A closed narrative about a test repair, held by the test itself.

page-guard-is-fingerprint-based.claim: An interstitial from a vendor the guard does not recognise is scored with a warning rather than refused, because it cannot be told from a client-rendered shell.
page-guard-is-fingerprint-based.why: The claim is about pages nobody has a fingerprint for. A probe would have to invent one, and inventing the input is how a check comes to test its own assumption.

privacy-and-trust-links-boundary.claim: A commenter's privacy link and contact route no longer count as the page's own: on the page this entry was measured on, both lists are empty.

rendered-artifacts-cannot-be-re-measured.claim: An operator-supplied artifact can be bounded by age and refused for naming another page, and nothing can verify what it says about itself.
rendered-artifacts-cannot-be-re-measured.why: Nothing executable is a witness: the limit is that a file's own claims cannot be re-measured, and `touch` exists. A probe here could only assert that the flag it already has still exists.

rendered-mobile-measures-owed.claim: The rendered artifact carries four mobile measures, and each is asserted by exactly one item: horizontal overflow by MB-107 and clipped text by MB-108, the two owed since 0.62.0.

russian-report-english-titles-as-first-w.claim: Superseded by the entry above it.
russian-report-english-titles-as-first-w.why: Kept deliberately as the entry the repair replaced.

russian-report-is-russian-throughout.claim: Every registry item carries a Russian title and a Russian recommendation, by id and not only by count.

te-179-and-go-134.claim: Closed, TE-179 in 0.21.0 and GO-134 in 0.23.0.
te-179-and-go-134.why: A closed narrative about two registry repairs, held by their assertions.

test-files-that-ran-part-of-themselves.why: A closed narrative about a suite repair, held by the discovery rules it fixed.

the-branded-query-is-whatever-got-the-mo.claim: KW-070 and GO-139 both read a `branded` block whose query is simply the highest-click query; nothing identifies a brand. On a property whose head term is generic and whose brand name has zero impressions, both items fail the site over a query that is not its brand.

the-crawl-defaults-now-decide-whether-it.claim: DEFAULT_MAX_PAGES = 100 and DEFAULT_DEPTH = 3 decide whether the fifteen crawl-fed items answer at all, and both are inherited. The probe used to count every truncation reporter under that name, which was seven items too many; the crawl-fed set is now derived from requires: crawl and the rest are recorded beside it.

the-other-caps-have-not-been-read.claim: All twenty-three scripts behind an assertion that passes by absence have been read against one question: does the cap stand upstream of the number the item reads. Twenty-one are downstream or have no cap; faceted_nav_audit.py under AR-163 and cache_compression_checker.py under TE-170 were upstream and now report truncation, and both numbers moved into module constants the threshold inventory can see.

cleared_by_reading.a11y_seo_checker.py: slices findings, not input, and CN-036 reads a contrast count instead
cleared_by_reading.domain_safety_check.py: slices error text; no input is cut
cleared_by_reading.entity_checker.py: head-checks the first three profiles, but GEO-006 reads the missing count, not those findings
cleared_by_reading.gsc_checker.py: GO-134 reads the sitemap report, which is not paged; the row and page caps sit on `performance`, which nothing asserts
cleared_by_reading.gsc_url_inspection.py: its only break ends a retry loop on success
cleared_by_reading.mobile_render_checker.py: counts every wide value, then slices the evidence list
cleared_by_reading.parse_html.py: the four items read whole fields; every slice is on evidence text
cleared_by_reading.rendered_audit.py: no cap; its one constant is a viewport width
cleared_by_reading.rich_results_guard.py: counts the whole `issues` before slicing the lines
cleared_by_reading.schema_required_props.py: counts errors and warnings whole, then slices the lines
cleared_by_reading.url_quality.py: no cap; its constants are the rule, not a limit on input

the-schema-property-tables-have-not-been.claim: schema_required_props.py carries required and recommended property tables for twenty-three types and reads as though it quoted Google. Two were examined in 0.89.0 and both diverged; the rest have not been read against the documentation they claim to follow.

verified_against_google.Article: diverges — Google documents no required properties for Article/NewsArticle/BlogPosting and does not list mainEntityOfPage or publisher among the recommended; read in 0.89.0 and deliberately not acted on
verified_against_google.WebSite: corrected in 0.89.0: name and url required, nothing recommended; the sitelinks search box is gone

threshold-declarations-unjudged.claim: The four shapes 0.71.0 singled out are judged and declared — the two MinHash constants and the three detect_profile tables as inherited, DEFAULT_MAX_REDIRECTS left outside as a fetch budget — and twenty module-level numeric constants carry no basis and are beyond the name-based scan.

title-polarity-has-no-gate.claim: Seventy-six of 217 items pass only when a path is absent or bounded, over nine spellings; whether a title states the side of its subject that its assertion means is read by a person, and the entry says why no check can.

titles-thinner-than-their-assertions.claim: AR-152 asserts that robots.txt has any user-agent group at all, and CN-056 asserts one date of any kind, while both titles promise more; MD-184's title was brought to its assertion in 0.85.0 and what an image-usage item should assert instead of `count gte 1` is still open.

verify-bots-and-the-default-claim.claim: Closed in 0.15.0; the default remains a claim, and says so.
verify-bots-and-the-default-claim.why: A closed narrative whose open half is a deliberate refusal to make a network call about a third party without being asked.

wasted-bytes-before-gzip.claim: The gzip survival rate was measured across 173 source/minified pairs, and `wasted_bytes` still multiplies raw bytes by the raw-byte savings fraction and reports against an uncompressed threshold.
